explanation: Maintain the best value for every capacity. For each item, compare skipping it with taking it after a solution for the remaining capacity. Update capacities downward so one item cannot be reused during the same iteration.
timeComplexity: O(nC) time for n items and capacity C. Every item-capacity state compares taking and skipping; descending one-row updates use O(C) rather than O(nC) storage.
spaceComplexity: O(C) auxiliary space. The one-row update keeps capacity+1 values; native recursion stores item/capacity states and its call chain.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: Before an item is processed, best[c] is the greatest value attainable with earlier items and capacity c. Descending capacity order ensures best[c−weight] still belongs to the earlier-item stage. Comparing skip and take therefore considers every legal subset without reusing the current item.
walkthrough: For items (weight,value) [(2,7),(3,9),(4,12)] and capacity 5, choosing the first two gives weight 5 and value 16. The last item alone gives only 12, so the answer remains 16. JSON arguments are [items,capacity], with each item [weight,value]. C#/JavaScript use pair records and native wrappers construct Item records.
edgeCases: An item is selected at most once, including a zero-weight item.
Capacity zero permits zero-weight items but no positive-weight item.
Skipping all items allows value zero even when values are negative.
Item records are (weight,value), not the reverse.
